what_it_does: Modern data centers often use solid-state drives (SSDs) that enforce a strict append-only rule: you can only write new data at the end of a zone, not overwrite the middle. When several such drives are grouped together for redundancy — a technique called RAID, where a parity (error-correction) record lets you reconstruct data if one drive fails — updating that parity record for a small partial write becomes awkward and slow, requiring extra writes to a separate bookkeeping area. Zebra sidesteps this problem by exploiting a small scratch buffer already built into each drive (called the Zone Random Write Area, or ZRWA) to absorb those parity updates in place, eliminating the bottleneck. The abstract suggests this approach improves performance under demanding workloads across different drive sizes without changing the drives themselves.
